correctness.rationale: Every positive primitive 2-cycle 0<u<v<1 satisfies u f(u)=v f(v), forcing equal values of unimodal H(x)=x^2(1-x)(c+mx). Symmetric division with s=u+v,p=uv gives p=s(s-1)(c+ms)/(c+m(2s-1)), then r=R(s)=[c+m(2s-1)]/[(s-1)(c+ms)(c+m(s-1))]. Discriminant equals -s[2ms²+3(c-m)s-4c]/[c+m(2s-1)], positive exactly s in (1,s*), where 1<s*<2 is the unique positive root. R strictly decreases from infinity to r*, thus precisely one unordered primitive 2-cycle for r>r* and none otherwise. Exact complementary product proves u,v lie inside (0,1). As s↓1, singular expansion yields c>0: ru→1/c and r²(1-v)→1/[c(c+m)]; c=0: sqrt(mr)u→1 and (mr)^(3/2)(1-v)→1. Symbolic elimination and boundary expansion independently reconstructed. Restriction to positive cycles, not a claim that all x∈[0,1] remain forward-invariant for all r.
